questions.q: To whom did the word of Yahweh come?
questions.a: The word of Yahweh came to Jeremiah.

questions.q: What does Yahweh remember about the people of Jerusalem?
questions.a: Yahweh remembers that the people of Jerusalem loved him in the past.

questions.q: What happened to those who harmed the people of Israel?
questions.a: Disaster came on them.

questions.q: What does Yahweh want the house of Jacob to tell him?
questions.a: Yahweh wants them to tell him what wrong he, Yahweh, did to their ancestors.

questions.q: Who brought the people up from the land of Egypt?
questions.a: Yahweh brought them up from the land of Egypt and led them through the wilderness.

questions.q: What did the people do after Yahweh brought them into a fruitful land?
questions.a: They defiled Yahweh’s land.

questions.q: For whom did the prophets prophesy?
questions.a: The prophets prophesied for Baal.

questions.q: With whom will Yahweh contend?
questions.a: Yahweh will contend with the people and with their grandchildren.

questions.q: Where does Yahweh tell the people to look to see if anything like this has happened?
questions.a: Yahweh tells them to look to Kittim and to Kedar.

questions.q: For what have Yahweh’s people exchanged their glory?
questions.a: Yahweh’s people have exchanged their glory for things that cannot help them.

questions.q: What does Yahweh tell the heavens to do?
questions.a: Yahweh tells the heavens to be appalled and to shudder.

questions.q: What two evils have Yahweh’s people committed?
questions.a: His people have abandoned the spring of living water and have dug for themselves broken cisterns that cannot hold water.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say Israel has become?
questions.a: Yahweh says Israel has become plunder for others.

questions.q: What did Israel’s enemies do to Israel?
questions.a: They roared against him like young lions and made his land a desolate place.

questions.q: What happened to Israel’s cities?
questions.a: His cities became ruins, and no one lived in them anymore.

questions.q: What did the people of Memphis and Tahpanhes do to Israel?
questions.a: They shaved the crown of Israel’s head.

questions.q: What did the people abandon?
questions.a: They abandoned Yahweh their God.

questions.q: What two nations do the people go to for help?
questions.a: They go to Egypt and to Assyria.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say the people have done that will bring punishment on them?
questions.a: They have done wicked things and turned away from Yahweh.

questions.q: What did the people say after Yahweh broke their yoke and tore their fetters?
questions.a: They said, “I will not serve!”

questions.q: What kind of vine did Yahweh plant?
questions.a: Yahweh planted a choice vine of good seed.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say remains even if the people wash themselves?
questions.a: Their guilt remains like a stain before him.

questions.q: What animal does Yahweh say the people are like?
questions.a: He says they are like camels and wild donkeys.

questions.q: What did the people say about foreign gods?
questions.a: They said they loved strangers and would go after them.

questions.q: What sin has caused the house of Israel to be ashamed?
questions.a: They are ashamed because they have worshiped trees and stones.

questions.q: What is Yahweh’s declaration?
questions.a: All of you have rebelled against me.

questions.q: Why does Yahweh say he has punished the people in vain?
questions.a: His punishment of them was in vain since they would not accept discipline.

questions.q: What do Yahweh’s people say about coming to him?
questions.a: They say they will roam free and will not come to him anymore.

questions.q: What have Yahweh’s people forgotten?
questions.a: They have forgotten Yahweh for many days.

questions.q: What are the people skilled at finding?
questions.a: They are skilled at finding other gods to love.

questions.q: What have the people done to the innocent and the poor?
questions.a: They have killed the innocent and the poor.

questions.q: Why do the people think that Yahweh’s anger will turn from them?
questions.a: The people think that they have not sinned.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say will happen to the people because of Egypt?
questions.a: They will be shamed by Egypt just as they were shamed by Assyria.

questions.q: What has Yahweh done to the ones the people trusted?
questions.a: Yahweh has rejected them.

commentary.text: God expostulates with his people. (Jer. 2:1-8) Their revolt beyond example. (Jer. 2:9-13) Guilt the cause of sufferings. (Jer. 2:14-19) The sins of Judah. (Jer. 2:20-28) Their false confidence. (Jer. 2:29-37)

Jer. 2:1-8 Those who begin well, but do not persevere, will justly be upbraided with their hopeful and promising beginnings. Those who desert religion, commonly oppose it more than those who never knew it. For this they could have no excuse. God's spiritual Israel must own their obligations to him for safe conduct through the wilderness of this world, so dangerous to the soul. Alas, that many, who once appeared devoted to the Lord, so live that their professions aggravate their crimes! Let us be careful that we do not lose in zeal and fervency, as we gain knowledge.

Jer. 2:9-13 Before God punishes sinners, he pleads with them, to bring them to repentance. He pleads with us, what we should plead with ourselves. Be afraid to think of the wrath and curse which will be the portion of those who throw themselves out of God's grace and favour. Grace in Christ is compared to water from a fountain, it being cooling and refreshing, cleansing and making fruitful: to living water, because it quickens dead sinners, revives drooping saints, supports and maintains spiritual life, and issues in eternal life, and is ever-flowing. To forsake this Fountain is the first evil; this is done when the people of God neglect his word and ordinances. They hewed them out broken cisterns, that could hold no water. Such are the world, and the things in it; such are the inventions of men when followed and depended on. Let us, with purpose of heart, cleave to the Lord only; whither else shall we go? How prone are we to forego the consolations of the Holy Spirit, for the worthless joys of the enthusiast and hypocrite!

Jer. 2:14-19 Is Israel a servant? No, they are the seed of Abraham. We may apply this spiritually: Is the soul of man a slave? No, it is not; but has sold its own liberty, and enslaved itself to divers lusts and passions. The Assyrian princes, like lions, prevailed against Israel. People from Egypt destroyed their glory and strength. They brought these calamities on themselves by departing from the Lord. The use and application of this is, Repent of thy sin, that thy correction may not be thy ruin. What has a Christian to do in the ways of forbidden pleasure or vain sinful mirth, or with the pursuits of covetousness and ambition?

Jer. 2:20-28 Notwithstanding all their advantages, Israel had become like the wild vine that bears poisonous fruit. Men are often as much under the power of their unbridled desires and their sinful lusts, as the brute beasts. But the Lord here warns them not to weary themselves in pursuits which could only bring distress and misery. As we must not despair of the mercy of God, but believe that to be sufficient for the pardon of our sins, so neither must we despair of the grace of God, but believe that it is able to subdue our corruptions, though ever so strong.

Jer. 2:29-37 The nation had not been wrought upon by the judgements of God, but sought to justify themselves. The world is, to those who make it their home and their portion, a wilderness and a land of darkness; but those who dwell in God, have the lines fallen to them in pleasant places. Here is the language of presumptuous sinners. The Jews had long thrown off serious thoughts of God. How many days of our lives pass without suitable remembrance of him! The Lord was displeased with their confidences, and would not prosper them therein. Men employ all their ingenuity, but cannot find happiness in the way of sin, or excuse for it. They may shift from one sin to another, but none ever hardened himself against God, or turned from him, and prospered.
